es: Distinguir el significado literal del implícito en réplicas cortas de la vida diaria y elegir la interpretación coherente con el contexto.

teaching.en: 'It's a bit cold in here' can be a hint that you should close the window, especially when everyone can see that it is open.
teaching.es: «Hace un poco de frío aquí» puede ser una indirecta para que cierres la ventana, sobre todo cuando todos ven que está abierta.
teaching.explanationEs: El hint no pide nada con palabras: la petición se deduce de la situación.
segments: 'It's a bit cold in here' can be a hint that you should
close the window, especially when everyone can see that it is open.
teaching.audioText: 'It's a bit cold in here' can be a hint that you should close the window, especially when everyone can see that it is open.

teaching.en: A remark such as 'Some of us have been working all morning' can imply that you have not helped, although it never says so.
teaching.es: Un comentario como «Algunos llevamos toda la mañana trabajando» puede dar a entender que tú no has ayudado, aunque no lo diga.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply es dar a entender sin afirmarlo; el hablante deja que el oyente saque la conclusión.
segments: A remark such as 'Some of us have been working all morning'
can imply that you have not helped, although it never says so.
teaching.audioText: A remark such as 'Some of us have been working all morning' can imply that you have not helped, although it never says so.

teaching.en: The literal meaning of 'Great timing' is positive, but her tone of voice shows that she is annoyed, so you have to read between the lines.
teaching.es: El significado literal de «Great timing» es positivo, pero su tono de voz muestra que está molesta, así que hay que leer entre líneas.
teaching.explanationEs: Read between the lines es deducir lo que no se dice; el tono y la situación contradicen las palabras.
segments: The literal meaning of 'Great timing' is positive, but her tone of voice
shows that she is annoyed, so you have to read between the lines.
teaching.audioText: The literal meaning of 'Great timing' is positive, but her tone of voice shows that she is annoyed, so you have to read between the lines.

teaching.en: His reply was 'I'll think about it', and anyone who could take the hint understood that he meant no.
teaching.es: Su respuesta fue «Lo pensaré», y quien supiera captar la indirecta entendió que quería decir no.
teaching.explanationEs: Take the hint es darse cuenta de lo que el otro sugiere sin decirlo abiertamente.
segments: His reply was 'I'll think about it', and anyone who
could take the hint understood that he meant no.
teaching.audioText: His reply was 'I'll think about it', and anyone who could take the hint understood that he meant no.

teaching.en: When people complain politely, the hidden message is often in the context, not in the words, so listen for what is left unsaid.
teaching.es: Cuando la gente se queja con educación, el mensaje oculto suele estar en el contexto y no en las palabras, así que escucha lo que queda sin decir.
teaching.explanationEs: Complain + about/to: aquí la queja es cortés y por eso se esconde en el contexto.
segments: When people complain politely, the hidden message is often in the context,
not in the words, so listen for what is left unsaid.
teaching.audioText: When people complain politely, the hidden message is often in the context, not in the words, so listen for what is left unsaid.

teaching.en: The underlying message of a polite refusal is rarely the literal one, which is why the same sentence can welcome or reject you.
teaching.es: El mensaje de fondo de un rechazo educado rara vez es el literal, por eso la misma frase puede acogerte o rechazarte.
teaching.explanationEs: Underlying es lo que hay debajo de la superficie: la intención real frente a las palabras exactas.
segments: The underlying message of a polite refusal is rarely the literal one,
which is why the same sentence can welcome or reject you.
teaching.audioText: The underlying message of a polite refusal is rarely the literal one, which is why the same sentence can welcome or reject you.

prompt.es: Elige qué quiere decir de verdad Ana con su frase en la fiesta.

choices.text: She is afraid of driving alone in the dark again.
She wants her friend to check the time for her.
She hopes that her friend will offer her a lift home.

feedback.es: Ana se pone el abrigo y comenta la hora delante de alguien con coche: lo literal es un dato, pero lo que sugiere es una petición indirecta de que la lleve.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que hace Ana y en quién tiene coche: la frase no pregunta la hora.

origin.text: At the end of a long party, Ana puts on her coat, looks at her watch and says to a friend who has a car, 'Well, it's getting late, isn't it?'

prompt.es: Completa: «El significado literal es sí, pero su tono claramente dice no.»

feedback.es: El significado literal es el de las palabras exactas; el contraste con el tono revela el implícito.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa «al pie de la letra».

origin.text: The ___ meaning of his words is yes, but his tone clearly says no.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su respuesta daba a entender que no nos ayudaría.»

answer.text: His reply implied that he would not help us

feedback.es: Imply va seguido de una oración con that: aquí el would not help expresa lo que la respuesta daba a entender.

hint.es: Empieza por His reply y sigue con el verbo que significa «dar a entender».

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué quería decir realmente la compañera de piso.

choices.text: That it was the narrator's turn to wash the dishes.
That she praised the narrator's talent for cooking.
That she wanted to cook the next meal herself.

feedback.es: La compañera mira los platos sucios y contrasta cocinar con fregar: la narradora descubre después que era un recordatorio educado de que le tocaba a ella.

origin.audio: My flatmate never says anything directly. Last night she was standing at the kitchen door, looked at all the dishes in the sink and said, Some people are very good at cooking and very bad at washing up. I laughed, because she was smiling, but the next morning I found out that she had been trying to tell me, politely, that it was my turn. Looking back, I should have taken the hint at once.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada réplica con lo que quiere decir de verdad.

pairs: It's a bit cold in here.
Some of us have been working all morning.

feedback.es: Cada réplica oculta una intención: una petición, un rechazo, una ironía y un reproche, y todas se deducen del contexto más que de las palabras.

pairs: It's a bit cold in here.
Some of us have been working all morning.

prompt.es: Elige la interpretación más coherente con la situación descrita.

choices.text: She needs a few days to decide about the bike.
She is politely refusing without saying no.
She is keen on the idea but too shy to say so.

feedback.es: Cambiar de tema y no volver a mencionarlo indica que I'll think about it es un rechazo cortés, no una petición de tiempo.

origin.text: When you ask your sister to lend you her bike for the weekend, she says, 'I'll think about it.' Then she changes the subject and never mentions the bike again.

prompt.es: Escucha al anfitrión y elige qué quiere de sus invitados sin decirlo.

choices.text: He wants them to stay for another drink.
He wants to check the bus timetable.
He would like them to start leaving.

feedback.es: La hora, su madrugón y los autobuses forman un mensaje de fondo: el anfitrión quiere que sus invitados se vayan, pero no lo dice.

origin.audio: Well, it's nearly midnight, and I have an early start tomorrow. It's been a lovely evening, hasn't it? The buses still run until one, I believe, and I do hope nobody has a long journey home.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué recurso convierte la despedida en una indirecta amable.

choices.text: He mentions his early start and the buses instead of asking them to go.
He thanks them three times for coming and offers more food.
He complains openly that the evening has been too long.

feedback.es: Habla de datos (madrugón, autobuses) en lugar de pedir que se marchen: así suaviza el mensaje y evita quejarse abiertamente.

origin.audio: Well, it's nearly midnight, and I have an early start tomorrow. It's been a lovely evening, hasn't it? The buses still run until one, I believe, and I do hope nobody has a long journey home.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su tono dejó claro que no le gustaba.»

feedback.es: El tono (o la voz) contradice la palabra interesting: el significado implícito se revela por cómo se dice, no por lo que se dice.

origin.text: I asked whether she liked the gift. 'It's very... interesting,' she replied, and her ___ made it obvious that she did not.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lee entre líneas antes de responder.»

answer.text: Read between the lines before you answer

feedback.es: Read between the lines es una expresión fija; before you answer añade el momento en que debes hacerlo.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué pretende la jefa con su frase final?

choices.text: To praise Dana's report and ask for even more detail.
To ask Dana politely to finish and let others speak.
To complain that nobody else has prepared anything.

feedback.es: Mirar el reloj y mencionar que todos tienen más puntos convierten el elogio en una petición cortés de que Dana termine.

origin.text: During a team meeting, the manager looks at the clock, then at Dana, who has been talking for ten minutes, and says, 'Thank you, Dana. That's really detailed, and I'm sure everyone has other points too.'

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué da a entender la jefa con su reacción.

choices.text: That she will decide about the idea next month.
That she is too busy today but very keen.
That she is not interested, although she avoids saying so.

feedback.es: Aplazar el tema a un trimestre lejano y ponerse a escribir un correo son señales de rechazo sin decirlo.

origin.audio: After hearing my idea, my boss said, Interesting. Let's come back to it next quarter. Then she opened her email and started typing.

prompt.es: Completa: «Esa pregunta era una indirecta para que nos fuéramos.»

feedback.es: Hint es la indirecta: sugiere sin pedirlo y, como dice la frase, nadie lo dijo de forma directa.

origin.text: That question was really a ___ for us to leave, although nobody said so directly.

es: Interpretar coletillas de misma polaridad como reto, burla o reproche y distinguirlas de las coletillas que piden confirmar un dato.

teaching.en: You didn't promise to pay for everything, did you? I'm asking because I need to confirm the total, and it is a genuine question.
teaching.es: No prometiste pagarlo todo, ¿verdad? Lo pregunto porque necesito confirmar el total, y es una pregunta de verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Frase negativa + coletilla afirmativa (polaridad opuesta): pregunta de verdad para confirmar un dato.
segments: You didn't promise to pay for everything, did you? I'm asking because
I need to confirm the total, and it is a genuine question.
teaching.audioText: You didn't promise to pay for everything, did you? I'm asking because I need to confirm the total, and it is a genuine question.

teaching.en: Oh, you're the expert now, are you? Her sceptical smile made it clear that she did not believe he knew what he was doing.
teaching.es: Vaya, ¿ahora eres tú el experto, eh? Su sonrisa escéptica dejó claro que no creía que él supiera lo que hacía.
teaching.explanationEs: Frase afirmativa + coletilla afirmativa (misma polaridad): no pregunta, muestra duda o burla.
segments: Oh, you're the expert now, are you? Her sceptical smile made it
clear that she did not believe he knew what he was doing.
teaching.audioText: Oh, you're the expert now, are you? Her sceptical smile made it clear that she did not believe he knew what he was doing.

teaching.en: You can fix it by yourself, can you? With the same polarity, the tag is a challenge rather than a real question.
teaching.es: ¿Puedes arreglarlo tú solo, eh? Con la misma polaridad, la coletilla es un reto y no una pregunta real.
teaching.explanationEs: La coletilla repite el auxiliar de la frase (can); al no cambiar de polaridad, deja de preguntar y reta.
segments: You can fix it by yourself, can you? With the same
polarity, the tag is a challenge rather than a real question.
teaching.audioText: You can fix it by yourself, can you? With the same polarity, the tag is a challenge rather than a real question.

teaching.en: Too lazy to cook, are you? Said with mock surprise, the question is a tease and not a request for information.
teaching.es: ¿Demasiado vago para cocinar, eh? Dicha con sorpresa fingida, la pregunta es una broma y no una petición de información.
teaching.explanationEs: Mock describe lo fingido: la sorpresa no es real; tease es la broma que se hace a alguien.
segments: Too lazy to cook, are you? Said with mock surprise, the
question is a tease and not a request for information.
teaching.audioText: Too lazy to cook, are you? Said with mock surprise, the question is a tease and not a request for information.

teaching.en: Turn the music down, will you? The baby is fast asleep, so this is not a genuine question but an impatient reproach.
teaching.es: Baja la música, ¿quieres? El bebé está profundamente dormido, así que no es una pregunta de verdad sino un reproche impaciente.
teaching.explanationEs: Después de un imperativo, will you? no pide permiso: añade prisa o reproche.
segments: Turn the music down, will you? The baby is fast asleep,
so this is not a genuine question but an impatient reproach.
teaching.audioText: Turn the music down, will you? The baby is fast asleep, so this is not a genuine question but an impatient reproach.

teaching.en: When the tag has the same polarity as the sentence, listeners usually hear doubt, mockery or reproach, so context decides whether the speaker wants to tease or to confirm.
teaching.es: Cuando la coletilla tiene la misma polaridad que la frase, el oyente suele percibir duda, burla o reproche, así que el contexto decide si el hablante quiere bromear o confirmar.
teaching.explanationEs: Resumen: polaridad opuesta = confirmar; misma polaridad = retar, bromear o reprochar.
segments: When the tag has the same polarity as the sentence, listeners usually hear doubt, mockery
or reproach, so context decides whether the speaker wants to tease or to confirm.
teaching.audioText: When the tag has the same polarity as the sentence, listeners usually hear doubt, mockery or reproach, so context decides whether the speaker wants to tease or to confirm.

prompt.es: La jefa de Sara necesita confirmar un dato. ¿Qué pregunta hace?

choices.text: You didn't sign the contract, did you?
You didn't sign the contract, didn't you?
You signed the contract, did you?

feedback.es: Una pregunta real lleva polaridad opuesta: frase negativa con coletilla afirmativa; con la misma polaridad la coletilla expresaría duda.

hint.es: Para preguntar de verdad, la coletilla cambia la polaridad de la frase.

origin.text: Sara's manager believes that Sara did not sign the contract, and she asks because she genuinely needs to know before the meeting starts.

prompt.es: Completa: «Vaya, ¿ahora eres tú el jefe, eh?»

feedback.es: La coletilla repite el auxiliar de la frase (you're = you are) y, al ser afirmativa, reta a Leo en lugar de preguntar.

hint.es: Repite el verbo auxiliar de you're.

origin.text: Leo has just started telling everyone what to do. 'Oh, you're the boss now, ___ you?' said Mia with a sceptical smile.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Puedes arreglar esa bici tú solo, eh?»

answer.text: You can fix that bike by yourself can you

feedback.es: La frase afirmativa con can y la coletilla can you forman un reto: el hablante duda de que pueda arreglarla solo.

hint.es: La coletilla final repite el auxiliar de la primera parte.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué hace la tía con su coletilla.

choices.text: She asks for real information about the race.
She expresses doubt while pretending to ask a question.
She praises his training and offers to join him.

feedback.es: Coletilla afirmativa tras frase afirmativa, sonrisa fría y Of course you have: la tía expresa duda, no pide información.

origin.audio: My brother announced at dinner that he was going to run a marathon next month. Nobody said anything for a moment, and then my aunt put down her cup and asked, You're going to run forty-two kilometres, are you? She was smiling, but her tone was anything but warm. My brother answered, Yes, and I've been training for months, and my aunt replied, Of course you have, dear. It was obvious that she did not believe a word of it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada coletilla con su intención.

pairs: Too lazy to walk, are you?

pairs.es: Burla por la pereza del otro

pairs: Oh, you're the expert now, are you?

feedback.es: La polaridad opuesta comprueba un dato; la misma polaridad se burla o reta; tras un imperativo, will you? pide con impaciencia.

pairs: Too lazy to walk, are you?

pairs.es: Burla por la pereza del otro

pairs: Oh, you're the expert now, are you?

prompt.es: Elige la coletilla que muestra duda en lugar de preguntar de verdad.

choices.text: You didn't finish it in ten minutes, did you?
You finished it in ten minutes, didn't you?
You finished it in ten minutes, did you?

feedback.es: Con la misma polaridad (afirmativa + did you) la coletilla reta; las otras dos, de polaridad opuesta, serían preguntas reales.

origin.text: Your friend says he finished a three-hour report in ten minutes. You don't believe him, so you answer with a tag.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué hace la hermana de Tom con su coletilla.

choices.text: She teases him about the work he has not finished.
She checks a fact that she genuinely needs to know.
She offers to finish the painting for him.

feedback.es: La pared a medio pintar desmiente la frase afirmativa: la coletilla have you? es una burla, no una pregunta real.

origin.audio: Tom spent the weekend saying that he would paint the kitchen by himself. On Sunday evening his sister walked in, looked at the half-painted wall and said, Finished already, have you? Tom did not answer, because he knew that she was not asking whether he had finished.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige por qué no responde Tom.

choices.text: He is angry that she came into the kitchen without asking.
He realises that her question was not a request for information.
He has not noticed that she was talking to him.

feedback.es: El narrador dice que Tom sabía que ella no preguntaba si había terminado: la coletilla era una burla, y por eso no hay respuesta.

origin.audio: Tom spent the weekend saying that he would paint the kitchen by himself. On Sunday evening his sister walked in, looked at the half-painted wall and said, Finished already, have you? Tom did not answer, because he knew that she was not asking whether he had finished.

prompt.es: Completa: «Así que te comiste toda la pizza tú solo, ¿eh?»

feedback.es: La coletilla repite el auxiliar del pasado simple (did) sin negación: misma polaridad, por tanto burla.

origin.text: So you ate the whole pizza alone, ___ you? Nobody believes that, so the tag sounds more like a tease than a question.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Demasiado cansado para ir a casa andando, ¿eh?»

answer.text: Too tired to walk home are you

feedback.es: La frase sin verbo principal hace que la coletilla are you? lleve la burla: no se espera información, sino una reacción.

prompt.es: Lee el intercambio. ¿Qué postura adopta Leo ante lo que dice Mia?

choices.text: He wants to confirm a detail he has forgotten.
He is impressed and asks how she did it.
He is sceptical and challenges her claim.

feedback.es: La coletilla de misma polaridad, las preguntas retóricas sobre las cuarenta páginas y el «lo creeré cuando lo vea» muestran escepticismo.

origin.text: Mia: 'I've finished the report.' Leo: 'You've finished the report, have you? All forty pages, in one afternoon? I'll believe it when I see it.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Baja la voz, ¿quieres? El bebé está profundamente dormido.»

feedback.es: Tras un imperativo, will you? añade prisa o reproche: no pregunta si el otro quiere, sino que lo pide con impaciencia.

origin.text: Keep it down, ___ you? The baby is fast asleep, and I have only just got him to sleep.

prompt.es: Escucha a la madre y elige qué actitud muestra ante lo que dice su hijo.

choices.text: She doubts him and expects to be convinced.
She is proud and wants to thank him.
She is curious about the homework he received.

feedback.es: La coletilla de misma polaridad y el comentario sobre la película indican duda: la madre espera pruebas, no quiere un dato.

origin.audio: You've done all the homework already, have you? That was quick, considering that you were watching a film an hour ago.

es: Interpretar indirectas, atenuaciones (not bad, a bit late) e ironía en textos y audios breves, identificando la pista que revela la intención.

vocabulary.es: atenuación, decir menos de lo que es

teaching.en: After the flood, Tom looked at the ruined kitchen and said with a straight face, 'We have a small problem', a classic understatement.
teaching.es: Después de la inundación, Tom miró la cocina destrozada y dijo con cara seria: «Tenemos un pequeño problema», una atenuación clásica.
teaching.explanationEs: El understatement dice menos de lo que es; with a straight face hace la broma más difícil de detectar.
segments: After the flood, Tom looked at the ruined kitchen and said with
a straight face, 'We have a small problem', a classic understatement.
teaching.audioText: After the flood, Tom looked at the ruined kitchen and said with a straight face, 'We have a small problem', a classic understatement.

teaching.en: 'You're a bit late,' said the boss to Leo, who had arrived two hours after the meeting started, and she used the phrase to downplay a serious problem.
teaching.es: «Llegas un poco tarde», dijo la jefa a Leo, que había llegado dos horas después de empezar la reunión, y usó la frase para quitar importancia a un problema serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Downplay es restar importancia; aquí a bit convierte dos horas en algo casi insignificante.
segments: 'You're a bit late,' said the boss to Leo, who had arrived two hours
after the meeting started, and she used the phrase to downplay a serious problem.
teaching.audioText: 'You're a bit late,' said the boss to Leo, who had arrived two hours after the meeting started, and she used the phrase to downplay a serious problem.

teaching.en: 'What a brilliant idea,' said Mia in a sarcastic voice when the plan failed, and nobody in the room thought that she meant it.
teaching.es: «Qué idea tan genial», dijo Mia con voz sarcástica cuando el plan falló, y nadie en la sala pensó que lo dijera en serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Brilliant es positivo en literal; sarcastic indica que quiere decir lo contrario.
segments: 'What a brilliant idea,' said Mia in a sarcastic voice when the
plan failed, and nobody in the room thought that she meant it.
teaching.audioText: 'What a brilliant idea,' said Mia in a sarcastic voice when the plan failed, and nobody in the room thought that she meant it.

teaching.en: The irony is that the cooking teacher burned the dinner, and he described it in a deadpan tone as 'a small mistake'.
teaching.es: La ironía es que el profesor de cocina quemó la cena, y lo describió con gesto impasible como «un pequeño error».
teaching.explanationEs: La irony es la diferencia entre lo esperado y lo ocurrido; deadpan es decirlo sin mostrar emoción.
segments: The irony is that the cooking teacher burned the dinner, and
he described it in a deadpan tone as 'a small mistake'.
teaching.audioText: The irony is that the cooking teacher burned the dinner, and he described it in a deadpan tone as 'a small mistake'.

teaching.en: The critic called the concert 'not bad', which is high praise from him, although his tongue in cheek style makes it easy to miss.
teaching.es: El crítico calificó el concierto de «no está mal», lo cual es un gran elogio viniendo de él, aunque su estilo en broma hace fácil no notarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Tongue in cheek indica que algo se dice en broma o con sorna; aquí not bad es elogio, no crítica.
segments: The critic called the concert 'not bad', which is high praise from
him, although his tongue in cheek style makes it easy to miss.
teaching.audioText: The critic called the concert 'not bad', which is high praise from him, although his tongue in cheek style makes it easy to miss.

teaching.en: A sarcastic remark is sharper than understatement, because the speaker wants the listener to feel the criticism behind the joke.
teaching.es: Un comentario sarcástico es más cortante que la atenuación, porque el hablante quiere que el oyente sienta la crítica que hay tras la broma.
teaching.explanationEs: Comparar ayuda a clasificar: la atenuación suaviza, el sarcasmo hiere y la ironía contrasta.
segments: A sarcastic remark is sharper than understatement, because the speaker
wants the listener to feel the criticism behind the joke.
teaching.audioText: A sarcastic remark is sharper than understatement, because the speaker wants the listener to feel the criticism behind the joke.

prompt.es: Elige qué quiere decir de verdad el profesor con su frase.

choices.text: It is only a small problem that will soon be solved.
It is a serious problem that he chooses to downplay.
It is a funny surprise that he is enjoying.

feedback.es: El aula inundada y la ventana rota contradicen a bit of a problem: el profesor usa una atenuación para quitar importancia a algo grave.

hint.es: Compara las palabras con los hechos: ¿encaja «un poco» con el desastre descrito?

origin.text: During a storm, the teacher looks at the flooded classroom and the broken window and says calmly, 'Well, that is a bit of a problem.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir «no está mal» de una película increíble es una atenuación.»

feedback.es: Understatement es decir menos de lo que se piensa: not bad ante una película increíble es un caso típico.

hint.es: Es el nombre de la figura que dice menos de lo que es.

origin.text: Saying 'not bad' about an amazing film is an ___, because it says much less than you really think.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La ironía es que el panadero nunca come pan.»

answer.text: The irony is that the baker never eats bread

feedback.es: The irony is that introduce un contraste entre lo esperado (un panadero come pan) y lo que ocurre.

hint.es: Empieza por The irony is that.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige cómo va realmente la mañana de la jefa.

choices.text: Perfectly: she is happy to welcome a new colleague.
Slowly: she is not interested in anything today.
Badly: she describes a crisis as a minor problem.

feedback.es: La impresora en llamas y el cliente gritando contradicen «a small problem»: la jefa atenúa una crisis para no dejarse llevar por el pánico.

origin.audio: Yesterday my new boss introduced me to the team. The printer had just caught fire, the client was shouting on the phone, and she turned to me and said, calmly, Welcome to the company. Just a small problem this morning. Later she admitted that she always downplays things when she is under pressure, because panic makes everything worse. I couldn't help laughing; it was the most honest welcome I've ever had.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opinó realmente el vecino del concierto.

choices.text: He found it boring and wanted to leave.
He loved it so much that he lost track of time.
He found it exciting but could not find his seat.

feedback.es: Decir que fueron las mejores dos horas de la semana, con gesto impasible y buscando la salida, es ironía: el concierto le pareció aburrido.

origin.audio: I asked my neighbour whether he enjoyed the concert. He said, deadpan, Oh, it was the best two hours of my week, although I spent most of them looking for the exit.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su significado real.

From a boy who usually criticises everything, that was high praise.

teaching.en: Is that all you're having for dinner? From a mother who has spent all afternoon cooking, this is rarely a question about quantity.
teaching.es: ¿Eso es todo lo que vas a cenar? Viniendo de una madre que se ha pasado toda la tarde cocinando, rara vez es una pregunta sobre cantidad.
teaching.explanationEs: La pregunta es literal por fuera, pero el mensaje implícito es «come más» o «¿no te gusta?».

teaching.en: 'Nobody ever asks for seconds these days,' she sighed, which was her way of trying to drop a hint without sounding critical.
teaching.es: «Hoy en día nadie repite plato», suspiró, que era su manera de soltar una indirecta sin parecer crítica.

answer.text: My mother asks whether that is all I'm having, so she is hinting that she wants me to eat more. My grandmother says that nobody ever asks for seconds these days, so she hopes that somebody will ask, and she would be pleased if we enjoyed her cooking. Uncle, I'm sorry that I've been busy, but I'll call more often, won't I?

origin.text: Cena familiar. Tres comentarios: a) tu madre dice «Is that all you're having?»; b) tu abuela dice «Nobody ever asks for seconds these days»; c) tu tío dice «Some relatives only call when they need something». Escribe en inglés (160–210 palabras): qué quiere decir cada uno y por qué, tu respuesta con tacto a tu madre y a tu abuela, y una respuesta al tío que termine con una question tag.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué insinúa el primo con su frase?

choices.text: That his brother only comes for the food, not the family.
That the food was cold by the time it was served.
That nobody thanked the cook for the free lunch.

feedback.es: La mirada al hermano que llegó tarde convierte la generalización en un reproche concreto: solo aparece cuando hay comida gratis.

origin.text: At the end of a noisy family lunch, a cousin looks around the table at the empty dishes, then at his brother, who arrived after the main course, and says, 'Some people only visit when there is free food.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Hoy en día nadie repite plato, y hay muchas sobras.»

feedback.es: Ask for seconds es pedir repetir plato; la consecuencia lógica es que sobren muchos restos de comida.

origin.text: Nobody asks for ___ these days, so there are lots of leftovers in the fridge.

prompt.es: Elige la coletilla correcta: «El postre estuvo buenísimo, ¿verdad?»

choices.text: The dessert was lovely, isn't it?
The dessert was lovely, wasn't it?
The dessert was lovely, was it?

feedback.es: La coletilla repite el verbo de la frase en pasado (was → wasn't it) y, al ser de polaridad opuesta, pide coincidir.
